references.text: God's first promise to Abraham that all the families of the earth shall be blessed 'in you', which is expanded in Gen 22:18 to 'in your offspring'.
God confirms that Abraham will become a great and mighty nation, and that all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.
The promise from Gen 22:18 is repeated to Isaac: all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in his offspring, because Abraham obeyed God's voice.
The promise is extended to Jacob: all the families of the earth shall be blessed in him and his offspring, in accordance with the promise given to Abraham.
Peter quotes directly the promise to Abraham that all the families of the earth shall be blessed in his offspring, and applies it to Christ.
Paulus points out that Scripture foresaw that the Gentiles would be justified by faith, and quotes the promise that all nations shall be blessed in Abraham.
Paul explains that the promises were given to Abraham and his offspring, who is Christ, directly connected to the promise in Gen 22:18 about blessing through Abraham's offspring.
The author refers to God's oath to Abraham as an unchangeable promise, confirmed by an oath, consistent with the context of Gen 22:16-18.
Theological contrast and parallel: The nations' reaction (fear vs. blessing) toward God's people.
Direct fulfillment of the promise: The nations recognize and bless God's people.
New Testament fulfillment: Mary as part of the blessed offspring through whom all families are praised.
Theological parallel: Obedience as a prerequisite for receiving God's blessing.
New Testament confirmation: The promise to Abraham is the gospel of justification for all nations.
